subject: Console: per-endpoint cost fingerprinting and SLA fallback playbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa@acme-analytics.com>, ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Console: per-endpoint cost fingerprinting and SLA fallback playbook

Team —

Following the spike Acme saw last week (attached screenshot), they asked for two pragmatic console features we should discuss for Q1 roadmap:

1) Per-endpoint cost "fingerprints" — a small, stable profile for each route/endpoint that surfaces the expected token mix, avg latency, and the dominant cost drivers so customers (and CS) can quickly triage outliers.
2) SLA-fallback / exception gating playbook — a console-level control to declare a fallback policy for routes (e.g., degrade to a compatible cheaper model, route to dedicated pool, or enable cached-prefix responses) plus an ops playbook and one-click snapshot for post-mortem.

Acme wants a clear path: UI surface + recommended alert thresholds + what data to show in a per-route view (they called out tokens-by-step, tail-latency histogram, and top 3 cost contributors). They also asked for an exportable "playbook snapshot" that includes the last 24h of traces and the active routing policy.

Ask: can we scope an MVP that is implementable within one sprint of infra work + one sprint of console UI? Key risks: metric cardinality and retention implications for per-endpoint telemetry.

I attached the Acme screenshot and a quick spec I sketched (fingerprint-spec-v1.md). Let's sync on minimal data model, aggregation windows, and the fallback policy options we can support safely.

Next steps I'd like:
- Product (Marissa): propose the MVP fields + UI sketch by EOD Thu
- Infra (Jonas/Hannah): quick feasibility note on telemetry cardinality and retention costs by Fri
- I'll loop Acme in for a 30-min alignment once we have a short spec

Thanks —
Rishi

-- 
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: per-endpoint cost fingerprinting and SLA fallback playbook

Thanks Rishi — this is a clear ask. A few quick clarifying questions before I draft an MVP: 

- For the "fingerprint," do we want a single canonical fingerprint per route (rolled up over last 7d) or sliding windows (1h/6h/24h) exposed in UI? The former is cheaper but less responsive.
- For "cost contributors," are we surface-level (model type, quantization, batching inefficiency) or also include upstream prompt/template differences (e.g., repeated context that blows token counts)?
- For the fallback playbook, do we want the console to be able to trigger policy changes (change routing) or just document & recommend actions for ops to run? (The former has control-plane implications.)

Proposed MVP (my current thinking):
- Fingerprint: one canonical fingerprint per route, recalculated daily, with quick stats for 1h/24h current snapshots
- Cost contributors: model class + median token-per-request + observed batching efficiency score (derived)
- SLA fallback: UI to select one of three pre-approved fallbacks (route-to-cheaper-model, enable-caching, divert-to-dedicated); action button is gated behind an allowlist (ops/admin roles) and generates an audit snapshot.

I'll mock a 2-screen UI and a short acceptance criteria doc by Thursday EOD. Jonas/Hannah — can you comment on the cardinality concerns and an estimate for the aggregation job? If costly, we can reduce to daily recalculation and sampled per-route histograms.

—Marissa

-- 
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Console & Observability
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: per-endpoint cost fingerprinting and SLA fallback playbook

Hi Rishi — thanks for driving this. A couple of things from Acme's side: 

- The spike we attached was caused by a batch job that accidentally re-sent 3k requests with long contexts (our bug). We still want the fingerprint because it should have made the anomaly obvious faster.
- For the playbook snapshot: can the export include the active model version and quantization metadata? We need that for audits.
- On gating: if possible we need a "dry-run" mode where recommended fallbacks are suggested but not applied automatically; we want control until we validate behavior.

We're happy to join a 30-min sync once you have the MVP spec. Our CS lead (ops@acme-analytics.com) will coordinate availability.

—Lisa
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: per-endpoint cost fingerprinting and SLA fallback playbook

Quick feasibility note: 

- Cardinality: per-route daily fingerprint is fine. Sliding hourly windows for every route will blow up ingestion unless we sample. 
- Retention cost: keeping 30d of daily fingerprints for all customer routes is low-cost; keeping 90d increases storage but still manageable. The heavy cost is per-request traces; we'll attach 24h snapshots only on demand (playbook snapshot) to avoid constant retention.
- Implementation plan (rough): infra work to add a daily aggregation job (2 weeks), a small telemetry index to store fingerprints (1 week), and API endpoints for the console (3 days). Console UI sprint: 1 week for mock->implement if acceptance criteria scoped tight.

I'll coordinate with infra-runbooks to ensure playbook snapshot generation is asynchronous and caps export size. We can support dry-run mode easily (policy recommendation engine without applying changes).

Jonas

Jonas Weber

I'll also attach the spec and the spike screenshot to the shared drive hub for tracking.

Closing the loop here —
Rishi
